deities: Thangching (Thangjing) - primary deity of Sanamahism worshipped at Moirang; progenitor of the Moilang dynasty, rides a Manipuri pony (gift from Lord Marjing)
Thangjing Leima (Koiren Leima) - his two eponymous consorts (per Wikipedia)
festivals: Moirang Lai Haraoba (Thangjing Haraoba) - annual ritual festival in the summer months (typically April-June; Meitei lunar month of Kalen), with archaic liturgical protocols managed by maibas and maibis; the Khamba Thoibi Jagoi classical dance reenacts Meitei cosmogony (per Wikipedia)
Khamba Thoibi Jagoi - the classical Meitei dance said to have been first performed at the temple by Khuman Khamba and Moirang Thoibi during the Lei Langba ritual

history.dynasty: Moirang dynasty (Moilang principality); the temple was the institutional heart of the independent Moirang kingdom before its integration into unified Manipur. Moirang kings derived sovereign legitimacy from being chief patrons of Thangjing, and coronation rituals required pilgrimage and submission to the deity at this site. The temple preserves and displays the royal attires of the 12th-century Moirang kings (per Wikipedia and the Illustrated Weekly of India, 1975).
history.period: Ancient; 12th-century associations (the Khamba-Thoibi epic of the Moirang Shayon and the preserved royal robes). The present temple complex continues pre-Hindu ritual traditions.
history.summary: NOT A HINDU TEMPLE - keep-or-drop decision needed. The Thangjing (Ibudhou Thangjing) Temple at Moirang, Bishnupur district is the primary seat of worship of Thangching, a deity of Sanamahism, the indigenous polytheistic religion of the Meitei civilisation - it is a Sanamahi site, not a Hindu temple. CSV correction: the actual town is Moirang, Bishnupur district (very close to the banks of Loktak Lake) - NOT Thoubal as the CSV states; the town error is documented across sources (Wikipedia, Bishnupur district website, National Sports University). The temple is one of the most culturally vital pilgrimage sites of the Imphal valley, deeply tied to classical Meitei literature, folklore and the socio-political history of the Moirang kingdom. The millennium-old legend of Khamba and Thoibi is closely associated with the site: the Khamba Thoibi Jagoi is traditionally said to have been first performed at the temple in front of the deity's image. The temple remains the institutional epicentre for pre-Hindu traditional religious rituals in the Imphal valley, coexisting with the region's later Vaishnavite Hinduism. Access caveat: since 2023, Meitei pilgrimages to the sacred Thangjing Hills have faced restrictions; the Committee on Protection and Preservation of the Historic Rights of Koubru and Thangjing Hill Ranges (CPPKT) has demanded pilgrimage access (verify current conditions before visiting). Identity certainty: high - Wikipedia's dedicated article, the Bishnupur district government site and Justdial's Moirang temple listings all agree on Moirang, Bishnupur.

name: Ebudhou Thangjing Temple
town_description: Moirang is a historic town in Bishnupur district, Manipur, about 45 km from Imphal on the Tiddim Road, very close to the banks of Loktak Lake. It was the seat of the independent Moirang kingdom and remains the cultural heart of pre-Hindu Meitei tradition (the ancient temple of the pre-Hindu deity Thangjing, the Khamba-Thoibi legend, and the INA memorial).
